# Results — Study 407 (Dark Cloud Cover & Piercing Line)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a Piercing
Line marks a bottom and the next day(s) rise; a Dark Cloud Cover marks a top and the next day(s)
fall** — tested as a clean event study on a fixed **30-name** basket (29 liquid US large-caps +
**SPY**). We detect every twin by the precise OHLC rule (gap beyond the prior extreme, close past
the prior body's midpoint but short of a full engulfing), enter the **next** open (one execution
lag), and measure the forward **1 / 3 / 5 / 10-day** return **signed by the pattern direction**
(long after a Piercing, short after a Dark Cloud), against the unconditional base rate. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, `auto_adjust=True` (total-return adjusted) — 29 long-listed US large-caps + SPY (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-06-18** (last bar; pulled 2026-06-21) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-18 (**21.5** years; 5,399 bars per name) |
| Fingerprint | `bf1d6cb7ca54` (sha1[:12] of basket closes) |
| Events | **2,342** twins (1,074 Piercing · 1,268 Dark Cloud) at H=1 |
| Detector / entry / costs | precise OHLC twin rule (gap beyond prior extreme, close past prior body midpoint, not a full engulfing, `min_body_frac=0.001`); enter the **next open**, exit close +H; **5 bps** one-way × 2 (round trip) + **50 bps/yr** borrow on the short (Dark Cloud) leg |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is 30 names *still trading* in 2026. A
> fixed surviving-names panel cannot include firms delisted after a bad run, which mildly tilts the
> long (Piercing) leg up. Crucially this bias works **against** our finding: it would *help* the
> bullish-reversal claim, yet the twins still anti-predict — so survivorship cannot explain the
> result away.

## The signal — signed forward return after every twin (long Piercing / short Dark Cloud)

The signed-return mean is tested against **zero** with a Newey-West **HAC t** (the inference-bar
number) and a plain one-sample *t*; `base (long)` is the unconditional long forward return over the
same bars (the always-up drift the bullish leg must beat); the placebo *p* is the share of 10,000
random-bar / coin-sign draws whose mean **beats** the observed one.

| horizon | n events | Piercing | Dark Cloud | signed mean | base (long) | win-rate | HAC *t* | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* | net |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 2,342 | 1,074 | 1,268 | **−0.078%** | +0.028% | 46.0% | **−2.57** | −2.82 | 0.998 | −0.179% |
| 3-day  | 2,341 | 1,074 | 1,267 | **−0.097%** | +0.141% | 47.2% | −1.91 | −1.81 | 0.960 | −0.200% |
| 5-day  | 2,341 | 1,074 | 1,267 | **−0.105%** | +0.253% | 48.2% | −1.49 | −1.49 | 0.924 | −0.210% |
| 10-day | 2,339 | 1,073 | 1,266 | **−0.069%** | +0.530% | 49.3% | −0.71 | −0.68 | 0.755 | −0.179% |

Read it carefully. The signed twin return is **negative at every horizon**, and at H=1 it is
**significantly wrong-signed** (HAC *t* = −2.57) — the pattern doesn't fail to predict the reversal,
it **predicts the opposite**. The win-rate is **below 50%** at every horizon, and the placebo *p*
near 1.0 means almost *every* random pick of the same many trades beats the twin mean. As the
horizon lengthens the loss fades toward noise (the market's always-up drift reasserts itself), but
the effect is never positive-significant. Far from clearing the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar *for the
reversal*, the only |*t*| ≥ 2 reading points the wrong way.

## Where the damage comes from — the Dark Cloud (bearish) leg

Splitting the signed return by leg is the whole story:

| horizon | Piercing leg mean | HAC *t* | win% | Dark Cloud leg mean | HAC *t* | win% |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | −0.033% | −0.78 | 47.0% | −0.116% | −2.85 | 45.1% |
| 3-day  | +0.110% | +1.38 | 51.0% | −0.272% | −3.98 | 44.0% |
| 5-day  | +0.306% | +3.01 | 54.3% | −0.453% | −4.86 | 43.1% |
| 10-day | +0.481% | +3.04 | 56.9% | −0.536% | −3.91 | 42.7% |

The **Dark Cloud** (bearish) leg is the killer: after the supposed top, stocks keep **going up**
(the short loses badly, HAC *t* down to −4.86 at 5 days). The **Piercing** (bullish) leg looks
positive over 5–10 days — but that is just the market's always-up drift: the unconditional long
return at 10 days is **+0.53%**, and the Piercing leg earns only **+0.48%**, i.e. it
**underperforms simply holding for a day**. There is no reversal alpha in either leg; the bullish
leg rides beta (and lags it) and the bearish leg fights it.

## Costs — they only deepen a hole that's already below zero

Each event is a fresh round trip: **5 bps one-way × 2** (in + out) plus **50 bps/yr** borrow on the
short share. The gross signed mean is already negative at every horizon, so costs simply make it
worse (net −0.179% to −0.210%). There is nothing to charge against.

## Myth check — does a trend / volume filter rescue the reversal? No.

The textbook says the twins are most reliable **after a trend** (Piercing after a downtrend, Dark
Cloud after an uptrend) and **on heavy volume**. We add each filter at H=1:

| filter | n events | signed mean | HAC *t* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| plain | 2,342 | −0.078% | −2.57 | 46.0% |
| + trend | 1,243 | −0.081% | −1.92 | 45.5% |
| + volume spike | 190 | −0.185% | −1.88 | 45.3% |
| + both | 128 | −0.011% | −0.09 | 48.4% |

Every filtered variant is **still negative or flat** with a sub-50% win-rate (the sub-2 *t*'s on the
filtered cuts are just the small samples — the volume filter throws away ~92% of events — not a sign
flip). The folk "only count it after a trend, on volume" caveat does not turn the reversal positive;
it just discards trades.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel where we **plant** a known day-after reversal (the day after a detected twin
gets an extra drift in the pattern's direction), the inference behaves exactly as it must:

| planted edge | events | signed mean | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.000** (no edge) | 910 | +0.021% | +0.47 | 0.313 | 50.2% |
| **+0.004** (planted reversal) | 904 | +0.414% | **+9.07** | 0.000 | 62.5% |

With **no** planted reversal the test sits at *t* ≈ 0.5 (it does not manufacture significance from a
random walk); a planted reversal lights up to *t* = 9.07 with a 62.5% win-rate. The harness **can**
detect a real day-after reversal — the real tape simply doesn't have one (it has the opposite).

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The signed twin return is **wrong-signed and significant at H=1** on the real
  tape (HAC *t* = −2.57), negative at every horizon, win-rate **below 50%**, placebo *p* ≈ 0.998.
  Far from clearing the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar *for the reversal*, the effect points the wrong way:
  there is no predictive reversal here. (The Piercing leg's positive 5–10-day return is pure beta —
  it underperforms the unconditional long drift.) Survivorship works *for* the bullish claim and
  still can't save it. **NONE.**
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The gross edge is negative before a cent of cost, so there is nothing to
  trade long-short; costs (round trip + borrow) only widen the loss to −0.18% to −0.21% per event.
  No capacity question even arises. **MIRAGE.**
- **A reliable reversal? — BUSTED.** The twins do not mark turns on liquid US large-caps: the Dark
  Cloud leg keeps rising and the Piercing leg merely rides (and lags) the market. Adding the textbook
  trend/volume filters doesn't flip it. The synthetic control proves the test *would* see a real
  reversal if one existed — so the negative finding is the genuine article, not a dead harness.
